configuration: Upstream P2 two-dimensional DG scalar advection of a cylinder (16x16 cells) through one rotation period as a fluid species of the vlasov app.
variant: ic/variant/value.txt changes r0 from 0.2 to 0.20000000000000007, exactly two upward binary64 ULP.
altbuild: run.sh altbuild runs the nominal inputs on the same pinned source compiled strict-IEEE with the same gcc (-O2, no -ffast-math, -ffp-contract=off, no -march=native: the build-ieee/ tree of the oracle image); a correct port compiled without fast-math or FMA contraction is exactly such a build, so its distance from the default -O3 -ffast-math -march=native build is the floor a candidate must be allowed.

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck on 2026-09-07: run.sh altbuild (same source, gcc -O2 strict IEEE: no -ffast-math, -ffp-contract=off, no -march=native (build-ieee/)) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py: all graded values within bound

altbuild.what: same source, gcc -O2 strict IEEE: no -ffast-math, -ffp-contract=off, no -march=native (build-ieee/)

warrant: The graded histories and frames follow the DG advection fluid species with a prescribed velocity field in two dimensions. In `rt_dg_advect_2x_p2.c`, `r0` (line 63) is the radius of the advected cylinder; the two-ULP variant therefore moves every graded value at the level of the arithmetic, while a wrong upwind advection flux or a wrong two-dimensional modal update changes them at order one. The bound atol=1e-11, rtol=1e-11 was set on 2026-09-06 from the calibration selfcheck on the x86 worker 136.114.2.6 (1 cpu, 4 GB, Docker): the two-ULP variant used at most 1.2e-4 of it and the strict-IEEE altbuild at most 1.6e-4 (worst files `q.gkyl` and `q.gkyl`), a headroom of about 6197x over the larger legitimate perturbation, while the faults named above move the graded values at order one.
